cards.title: Mitten-code lifted-product check matrices
cards.statement: Expand A=[a0,a1] and B=[b0,b1] over F2[G] through L(g)|h>=|gh> and R(g)|h>=|h g^{-1}>; assemble H_X and H_Z as Eq. (2).

checks.detail: The PDF specifies the group IDs, four three-term ring supports, regular-representation conventions, and complete H_X/H_Z block layout.
L(a)R(b)=R(b)L(a) and L(a*)=L(a)^T, R(b*)=R(b)^T make the two terms of H_X H_Z^T equal; they cancel over F2.
Each check row meets three ring entries of weight three, hence has check weight nine before any accidental cancellation; the printed supports contain distinct elements.

open_questions: Table XIII uses zero-based positions in GAP Elements(G), inferred from the presence of index 0. With the paper-cited GAP 4.16.0 and SmallGrp 1.5.4, this literal interpretation makes the (60,11) pivot blocks singular and therefore exposes a paper/input-consistency question rather than closing every target invariant.

cards.title: Canonical logical basis from square invertibility
cards.statement: For e_g, solve R(b1)u_g=R(b0)e_g and L(a1)v_g=L(a0)e_g over F2; X_g=(e_g,u_g,0,0,0), Z_g=(e_g,0,v_g,0,0).

checks.detail: The paper prints both linear systems and identifies a1,b1 as the invertible pivot entries.
Substitution gives H_Z X_g^T=0 and H_X Z_g^T=0; minus equals plus over F2.
X_g and Z_h overlap only on D1, so their binary symplectic pairing is delta_g,h.

cards.title: Block length, dimension, and 20 percent rate
cards.statement: For r1=r2=1,c1=c2=2, n=5|G| and k=n-rank(H_X)-rank(H_Z)=|G| when both two-row-block check matrices have rank 2|G|.

checks.detail: The block-count and rank formulas are explicit.
The five data blocks give n=5|G|; four independent check blocks give k=|G| and k/n=1/5.

open_questions: Full check-matrix ranks are independently recomputed rather than assumed from the claimed parameters.

checks.detail: Eq. (E15) prints all three closed forms and Table V gives the evaluation grid.
n-N_X-N_Z=|G|, matching the number of injected logical qubits.
All counts are integer multiples of the group order and remain positive for d_rep>=1.

cards.title: sQetch random sketched information-set decoding
cards.statement: Sample kappa null-space basis rows with replacement, randomly permute columns, RREF the sketch, and retain the lightest nontrivial logical row as Algorithm 1 prescribes.

checks.detail: The PDF provides the inputs, sampling law, column permutation, RREF loop, logical test, and candidate selection.
Row operations preserve the sampled null-space span, and undoing the column permutation returns every candidate to the original coordinates.
The implementation must recover distance three on the [[7,1,3]] Steane CSS code before any mitten-code benchmark is accepted.

open_questions: The paper does not publish exact benchmark candidate matrices, sketch sizes for Fig. 8, CPU model, or random seeds, so T003 is explicitly reduced-scale rather than paper-exact.

cards.title: sQetch hit-probability model
cards.statement: P_sketch follows inclusion-exclusion (H9), while Eqs. (H11)-(H13) estimate the conditional RREF exposure and total hit probability.

checks.detail: The exact inclusion-exclusion expression and stated approximations are printed.
The exact P_sketch lies in [0,1], vanishes for kappa=0 when j*>0, and reaches one as repeated sampling covers every required basis row.

open_questions: H11-H13 rely on the paper's generic pivot-set assumptions and are treated as a model check, not an exact theorem for every matrix.

cards.title: Real-time decoder utilization and reaction time
cards.statement: rho_i=f_i t_i/T_cyc and mean reaction time t_bar=sum_i f_i t_i, using the mean rather than worst S4 time in t_bar.

checks.detail: Eq. (I1), T_cyc=1 ms, the stage fractions, and stage times are printed.
f is dimensionless, rho is dimensionless, and f*t sums to a time.
Recomputation from rounded table inputs should agree with printed rho and t_bar within disclosed rounding tolerance, not exactly at hidden precision.

open_questions: The printed f and t values are rounded, so their direct sum need not equal the reported t_bar in the last digit.
